Healthy ecosystems provide important “services,” like clean air and water, healthy forests and farms, and habitat for our plants and animals. British Columbia contains a diverse range of ecosystems that support thousands of individual plant and animal species.

An ecosystem is a collection of communities of both living and non-living things that are connected. The biotic elements in an ecosystem include living things such as plants and animals. The abiotic elements found in an ecosystem include non-living things like land forms or climate.

Terrestrial ecosystems are found on land and include vegetation, ecosystems, soil, terrain and wildlife habitat.

details.column_comments: Element Global Id is a unique value for this element as it occurs globally.

Element Subnational Id is a unique value for this element as it occurs subnationally (provincially).
ELCODE, or Element Code is an alternate unique identifier for each Element in the CDC database. The first 10 characters identify the species/plant community.
Taxonomic Level  is the level of the element in the taxonomic hierarchy. Examples are species, subspecies, population, or variant.
Taxonomic Phylum is the phylum the element belongs to.
Taxonomic Class is the Class the element belongs to.
Class English is the Taxonomic class, in English, to which the species belongs. For example, Monocots, Dicots, Mammals, Birds, Reptiles, Insects.
Taxonomic Order is the Order the element belongs to.
Taxonomic Family is the Family the element belongs to.
Name Type Code is a code describing the Name Type an element belong to. Examples are A = Animal, P = Plant, C = Ecological Community.
Element Type desribes the element in the following groups:Vertebrate Animal, Invertebrate Animal,  Vascular Plant, Nonvascualr Plant, and Terrestrial Community - Other Classification.
GNAME is the Global Scientific Name of the element.
Global Common Name is the Global Common English name of the element, written in title case.
SNAME is the Scientific name of the element, written in sentence case.
Formatted SNAME is the RISC (Resource Information Standard Committee) standard Scientific name, including html tags for italics.
SNAME Author is Scientific Name Author.
SCOMNAME is the Subnational Common English name of the element, written in title case.
Formatted SCOMNAME is the RISC standard English common name of the element, including html tags for italics.
Global Rank is the global conservation status rank for the species or natural plant community, assigned by NatureServe International.
The Global Rank Change Date is the date on which the Global Conservation Status Rank for the Element was either initially entered or last changed.
The Global Rank Review Date is the date on which the Global Conservation Status Rank for the Element was last reviewed (i.e., assigned, reaffirmed, or changed).
Subnational Rank is the sub-national (provincial) conservation status rank for the species or natural plant community, assigned by the CDC.
The Subnational Rank Change Date is the date on which the Provincial Conservation Status Rank for the Element was either initially entered or last changed.
The Subnational Rank Review Date is the date on which the Provincial Conservation Status Rank for the Element was last reviewed (i.e., assigned, reaffirmed, or changed).

LIST is the provincial "list" status for this species or natural plant community. Possible values are; RED, BLUE, YELLOW, INTRODUCED, ACCIDENTAL, EXTINCT and SPECIAL. SPECIAL records include record sized trees.
Cosewic Comment is the comment associated with the attribute COSEWIC_CD.
COSEWIC_CD is the Committee on the Status of Endangered Wildlife in Canada designation for this element ( http://www.cosewic.gc.ca/)
COSEWIC Date is the date the Cosewic Code was granted.
CDCTrack specified whether this element is tracked by the CDC. Values are Y or N(null).
Endemism is a flag indicating whether the element is endemic to BC. Possible values are Y or N(null).
Breeding is a flag that Indicates whether a species Breeds in BC or uses the province only as a migratory corridor or wintering habitat. Possible values are Y or N(nul).
Identified Wildlife Code indicates whether the element has Subnational protection via Identified Wildlife. Possible values are Y or N(null).
Identified Wildlife Date is the date the Identified Wildlife Status was granted.
Identified Wildlife Comment are comments relevant to the Identified Wildife Code  (IDENT_WILDLIFE_CD)
Accidental ID is the numeric value of the accidental status of the element in BC.  ID Values/Descriptions  are: 1 - Regularly occurring,2 -Accidental/Nonregular, 3 - Unknown/Undetermined
Exotic ID is the ID describing the element's exotic status to  BC.  Possible ID /Description options are: 1 -Native, 2 - Exotic, 3 -Unknown/Undetermined.
The Order Sequence Number is an index value  used to sort elements by Taxonomic Orders phylogenetically.
The Family Sequence Number is an index value used to sort elements by Taxonomic Families phylogenetically.
The RISC (Resource Information Standards Committee) Code is a unique code for a plant or animal species, based on it scientific or common name.
EO Exists is a flag that indicates whetherthe CDC have any Element Occurrences (EOs) recorded for this element. Possible values are Y or N(null).

details.column_comments: CDC SR SYSID is a system generated unique identification number.
SCIENTIFIC NAME in the scientific name written in sentence case, e.g., Erythranthe suksdorfii.
ENGLISH NAME is the Common English name written in title case, e.g., Suksdorf's monkey-flower.
ELEMENT SUBNATIONAL ID is a unique identifier for all elements that occur subnationally (provincially), e.g., 20166.

DISTRIBUTION INFORMATION is a description that contains information about a species' or ecological community's range.  For species, the description contains spatial distribution information for a specific Ecosection. For ecological communities, the description contains information about how Biogeoclimatic Units were customized to produce a custom range. For example, 'Individuals are located in low elevations within this Ecosection' or 'This ecological community occurs within 1 km of the coast'.
DATA REFERENCE is a reference to the data or information used to determine whether an Ecosection (for species) or a Biogeoclimatic Unit (for ecological communities) is included in a range.
PRESENCE CATEGORY CODE is a code indicating the level of confidence that a species occurs within an Ecosection, e.g., 1 (Present), 2 (Presence Expected), 3 (Historical).
PRESENCE CATEGORY DESCRIPTION is a description of the Presence Category Code, i.e., Present (1), Presence Expected (2), Historical (3).
SEASONALITY contains the season(s) that the species is found or expected to be found within an Ecosection. Multiple species will be separated by semicolon, e.g., All, Spring, Summer, Fall, Winter.
VERSION DATE is the date of the current version of the species' or ecological community's range, i.e., the date that this range was first completed, or since then, comprehensively revised.
ELCODE is an alternate unique identifier for each Element in the BC Conservation Data Centre (CDC) database. The first 10 characters identify the species/ecological community, e.g., PGPIN01010.
ECOSECTION CODE is a unique three letter code for each Ecosection, e.g., TEB, PEP.
ECOSECTION NAME is the full name of the Ecosection, e.g., Whitehorse Upland, Tatshenshini Basin.
ECOSECTION_VERSION is the version of the Ecosection polygon line work that the ranges are based on, e.g., 2.01
PARENT ECOREGION CODE is the code for the Ecoregion that completely contains the Ecosection, e.g., CMI, NUP.
ELEMENT TYPE CODE is a description of the high-level category of life the observed species belongs to, i.e., A (Animal), P (Plant), C (Ecological Community).

ELEMENT TYPE identifies the element (species or ecological community) as belonging to one of the following groups: Vertebrate Animal, Invertebrate Animal, Vascular Plant, Nonvascular Plant, Alga, Terrestrial Community - Other Classification, Other (Botanical).
SPECIES CODE is a standard code for a plant or animal species, based on its scientific or common name, e.g., M-URAR (Ursus arctos).
TAXONOMIC CLASS is the taxonomic class, in English, to which the species belongs, e.g., Monocots, Dicots, Mammals, Birds, Reptiles, Insects.
ECOSYSTEM GROUP is a classification of ecological communities into broad ecosystem types, e.g., Terrestrial - Alpine: Alpine.
GLOBAL RANK is the global conservation status rank for the species or ecological community, assigned by NatureServe International, e.g., G3G4.
GLOBAL RANK CHANGE DATE is the date that the status rank for the species or ecological community was changed.
GLOBAL RANK REVIEW DATE is the date that the status rank for the species or ecological community was reviewed.
PROVINCIAL RANK is the sub-national (provincial), conservation status rank for the species or ecological community, assigned by the CDC, e.g., S3S4.
PROVINCIAL RANK CHANGE DATE is the date that the status rank for the species or ecological community was changed.
PROVINCIAL RANK REVIEW DATE is the date that the status rank for the species or ecological community was reviewed.

COSEWIC CODE is a code indicating the COSEWIC (Committee on the Status of Endangered Wildlife in Canada) designation for the observed species, e.g., E (Endangered), XX (Extinct), XT (Extirpated), T (Threatened), SC (Special Concern), NAR (Not at Risk), DD (Data Deficient).
COSEWIC COMMENTS contains comments about the COSEWIC (Committee on the Status of Endangered Wildlife in Canada) assessment.
COSEWIC DATE is the date of the COSEWIC (Committee on the Status of Endangered Wildlife in Canada) assessment.
BC LIST is the provincial 'list' status for the species or ecological community, i.e., Red, Blue, Yellow, Accidental, Exotic, Extinct, No Status, Unknown or N/A.
SARA SCHEDULE is the SARA (Species at Risk Act) schedule number for this element, e.g., 1.
SARA STATUS is the SARA status for the species, i.e., E (Endangered), XX (Extinct), XT (Extirpated), T (Threatened), SC (Special Concern), NAR (Not at Risk), DD (Data Deficient).
SARA DATE is the SARA (Species at Risk Act) date of listing.
SARA COMMENTS contains comments about the SARA (Species at Risk Act) listing.

IDENTIFIED WILDLIFE CODE is a code that indicates whether the observed species or ecological community has sub-national protection under FRPA (Forest Range and Practices Act), i.e., Y (Yes), N (No) or Null.
IDENTIFIED WILDLIFE DATE is the date of listing under FRPA (Forest Range and Practices Act).
IDENTIFIED WILDLIFE COMMENTS contains comments about the species' listing under FRPA (Forest Range and Practices Act).

LAND USE OBJECTIVES Orders define red- and blue-listed ecological communities for Ecosystem Based Management (EBM) Implementation. LUO orders are not province wide. These definitions do not match CDC red- and blue-listed ecological communities exactly and CDC updates may not be reflected in the Schedules of each EBM Land Use Objectives Order, e.g., HG or CNC; SCC.
ENDEMISM is a flag indicating whether the observed species or ecological community is endemic to BC, i.e., Y (Yes), N (No), P (Probable), or NULL.
WILDLIFE ACT STATUS is a field that contains the status of a species listed as 'Endangered' or 'Threatened' under the Provincial Wildlife Act, i.e., Endangered, Threatened or Null.
BIOGEOCLIMATIC UNIT is a semicolon separated value list of Biogeoclimatic (BGC) Units that apply to the element, e.g., IDFxm; BGxw2; IDFdk3.
BIOGEOCLIMATIC VERSION is the version of Biogeoclimatic (BGC) mapping used in the field Biogeoclimatic Unit, e.g., 9.
CDC TRACK is a flag that indicates whether the Conservation Data Centre tracks this element or not, i.e., Y, N, P, W, Null.
ELEMENT OCCURRENCE EXISTS is a flag indicating whether the Conservation Data Centre has any Element Occurrences (EOs) recorded for the observed species, i.e., Y (Yes), N (No), or Null.
BCSEE REPORTS REFS URL contains the URL that links to the available reports and references for each species or ecological community.
FEATURE_AREA_SQM is the system calculated area of a two-dimensional polygon in square meters.
FEATURE_LENGTH_M is the system calculated length or perimeter of a geometry in meters.
SHAPE is the column used to reference the spatial coordinates defining the feature.
OBJECTID is a column required by spatial layers that interact with ESRI ArcSDE. It is populated with unique values automatically by SDE.
SE_ANNO_CAD_DATA is a binary column used by spatial tools to store annotation, curve features and CAD data when using the SDO_GEOMETRY storage data type.

If you do not find an element occurrence in your area of interest, this means there are none currently mapped in the CDC database. The best way to verify whether an area contains a species or ecosystem at risk is to have do a detailed assessment of the property during the appropriate season.

organization.description:
Healthy ecosystems provide important “services,” like clean air and water, healthy forests and farms, and habitat for our plants and animals. British Columbia contains a diverse range of ecosystems that support thousands of individual plant and animal species.

An ecosystem is a collection of communities of both living and non-living things that are connected. The biotic elements in an ecosystem include living things such as plants and animals. The abiotic elements found in an ecosystem include non-living things like land forms or climate.

Terrestrial ecosystems are found on land and include vegetation, ecosystems, soil, terrain and wildlife habitat.

organization.title: Ecosystems
organization.description:
Healthy ecosystems provide important “services,” like clean air and water, healthy forests and farms, and habitat for our plants and animals. British Columbia contains a diverse range of ecosystems that support thousands of individual plant and animal species.

An ecosystem is a collection of communities of both living and non-living things that are connected. The biotic elements in an ecosystem include living things such as plants and animals. The abiotic elements found in an ecosystem include non-living things like land forms or climate.

Terrestrial ecosystems are found on land and include vegetation, ecosystems, soil, terrain and wildlife habitat.
